When BPF_FETCH is set
column2: atomic instructions load a value from memory

column1: into a register. The current verifier code first checks via
check_mem_access whether we can access the memory
via check_reg_arg whether we can write into the register.
For loads
column2: check_reg_arg has the side-effect of marking the

column1: register's value as unkonwn
column2: and check_mem_access has the side effect

column1: of propagating bounds from memory to the register. This currently only
takes effect for stack memory.
Therefore with the current order
but by simply reversing the order of check_reg_arg
vs. check_mem_access
column2: we can instead propagate bounds smartly.

column1: A simple test is added with an infinite loop that can only be proved
unreachable if this propagation is present. This is implemented both
with C and directly in test_verifier using assembly.
